item.title: Cheerio vs jsdom vs parse5 in 2026: Which Node.js HTML Parser Should You Use?
item.description: Every web scraper, test runner, and static analyzer in the Node.js ecosystem eventually has to turn raw HTML into something you can query — and the library you pick changes your throughput by an order of magnitude. The three contenders in 2026 are Cheerio (30,475 GitHub stars), jsdom (21,664), and parse5 (3,928) — all MIT-licensed, all actively maintained with commits this week. They look interchangeable from the outside, but they are built for completely different jobs: one is a fast jQuery-style scraper, one is a full browser DOM, and one is the low-level spec parser hiding underneath both of the others. Pick the wrong one and you either execute untrusted code you should not, or ship a scraper that is ten times slower than it needs to be.

item.title: HTML Sanitizer Libraries for XSS Prevention: Bleach vs HTML Purifier vs sanitize-html vs NH3
item.description: User-generated content is the lifeblood of modern web applications — comments, forum posts, rich text editors, and markup previews all accept HTML input from untrusted sources. Every piece of user-submitted HTML is a potential Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attack vector. HTML sanitizer libraries act as the last line of defense, stripping malicious code while preserving safe formatting.
